Iowa To Make It A Felony To Give Away Marijuana:
"We need to be a little bit tough on some of these kids
because maybe they don’t have the structure at home that our kids do."

April 16, 1999
From The Des Moines Register
http://www.dmregister.com/
By Jonathan Roos, Register Staff Writer
See

SENATE HARDENS POT-SALE PENALTY

Had he been able to vote from the Senate gallery Thursday, Iowa State University senior Brian Dirks said, he would have supported tougher marijuana penalties.

Dirks, a forestry major from Le Mars, and six ISU companions watched the Senate debate, then approve a bill that would make it a felony to sell even the smallest quantity of marijuana.

Opponents argued that the stricter law could damage the future of a young adult who makes a mistake. But Dirks said offenders should pay the consequences. "I’d be real scared if someone was going to law school or medical school using drugs," he said.
(Marijuananews note: But not real literate? Maybe he should change from forestry to journalism. Why is a forestry major’s opinion cited here? Is it typical of the student body at ISU?
See
College Freshman Survey Indicates Increasing "Conservatism"--
"Less than 33 percent support legalization of marijuana."
Little Change From Last Year, But Way Up From 17% Ten Years Ago!

Of course, never mind that there are former marijuana smokers on the Supreme Court, (Clarence Thomas, who smoked while at Yale Law School) and in the highest offices in federal and state governments, this bill is not about use, but small scale, "accommodation" sales. It will only be used if the police are wasting resources, or extorting testimony. Just what Iowa needs.)

The bill also would increase criminal penalties to a maximum five years in prison for someone who gives one-half to 1 ounce of marijuana to another person.

Sen. Jeff Lamberti, R-Ankeny, who guided debate of the bill, said it treats marijuana more like other illicit drugs. Critics said more punishment was the wrong approach. They called for more drug treatment and education.

"I don’t think we want to fill up our prisons with more and more young people who make that mistake," said Sen. Johnie Hammond, D-Ames.

"The real problem is the meth problem," said Sen. Matt McCoy, D-Des Moines.

Supporters of the bill rejected those arguments. "I know meth is getting all the headlines, but there is a drug problem and marijuana is part of it," said Sen. David Miller, R-Libertyville.

Said Sen. Mike Sexton, R-Rockwell City, "We need to be a little bit tough on some of these kids because maybe they don’t have the structure at home that our kids do."

(Marijuananews note: That is one of my favorite arguments for sending kids to prison, punishing them for not having structure at home. We are governed by truly appalling people.)

The bill, passed on a 34-11 vote, already had sailed through the House. It still needs Gov. Tom Vilsack’s signature to take effect.
